steps.label: KP02 Data are vectors, models are mappings
Data are vectors, models are mappings · 1/9
steps.speakerNotes: KP01 left a question: what does a model receive? This unit fixes how data is represented. (The apple is an analogy, not the note's data.)

steps.label: Data are vectors, models are mappings · 1/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: One apple is one sample.

steps.label: Data are vectors, models are mappings · 1/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: It can have many measurements: sweetness, crunchiness, size. Each measurement is a feature. The bars are a sketch with no real numbers.

steps.label: Data are vectors, models are mappings · 1/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: A model needs values in a fixed order with the same meaning; sweetness cannot come first in one sample and crunchiness first in the next.

steps.label: A fixed coordinate order · 2/9
steps.speakerNotes: A feature vector arranges one sample's values in a fixed order; with d features it has d coordinates. (Sweetness and crunchiness are a sketch with no numbers.)

steps.label: A fixed coordinate order · 2/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The first two samples both put sweetness first and crunchiness second.

steps.label: A fixed coordinate order · 2/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The third swaps the order: the same position now means something different, which confuses the model.

steps.label: A fixed coordinate order · 2/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Each coordinate position must keep its meaning. They share a numerical representation, not common units.

steps.label: Images and encoding · 3/9
steps.speakerNotes: Another example: an image. The source's 64×64 grayscale image has 64 times 64 equals 4096 pixels; only an 8×8 sketch is drawn.

steps.label: Images and encoding · 3/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Each pixel's grayscale level is a number.

steps.label: Images and encoding · 3/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Flatten them into a vector with 4096 coordinates. Image size is not the sample count; this is still one sample.

steps.label: Images and encoding · 3/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Also, words like red or elongated are descriptions, not yet real coordinates; the encoding must be specified.

steps.label: The data matrix · 4/9
steps.speakerNotes: With one sample defined, collect several. Each sample is a d-by-1 column; n samples side by side form a d-by-n data matrix. Rows are horizontal, columns vertical.

steps.label: The data matrix · 4/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The source has 12 unitless two-dimensional teaching points. Here are the first 3: (1.5, 2.0), (2.5, 2.5), (2.0, 3.5). (Teaching points, not real fruit.)

steps.label: The data matrix · 4/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Each column is one sample; a row is one feature. The ellipsis stands for 9 more samples, not another feature.

steps.label: The data matrix · 4/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The full matrix has 2 rows and 12 columns: 2 by 12.

steps.label: Rows or columns · 5/9
steps.speakerNotes: This is a supplement: software also often uses n-by-d arrays with samples in rows.

steps.label: Rows or columns · 5/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: This note's convention: samples in columns, shape d by n.

steps.label: Rows or columns · 5/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Common arrays use the opposite convention. It is not a mistake, but it differs from this note.

steps.label: Rows or columns · 5/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Always check shapes before matrix multiplication rather than assuming the first dimension counts samples.

steps.label: A model is a mapping · 6/9
steps.speakerNotes: A model is a family of functions indexed by theta, mapping a d-dimensional input to a p-dimensional output. Fixing theta selects one concrete function.

steps.label: A model is a mapping · 6/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The source example takes d equal to 2: two input numbers.

steps.label: A model is a mapping · 6/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The model has 2 weights and 1 offset: 3 parameters, together called theta.

steps.label: A model is a mapping · 6/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The output has p equal to 1: one score. p is output dimension, theta is the parameters; they differ, and p need not equal a class count.

steps.label: Substitute and compute · 7/9
steps.speakerNotes: The source's weighted-sum model: f equals w1 times x1 plus w2 times x2 plus b. Weights set each feature's contribution; b shifts every score. Defaults: w1 and w2 are 1, b is 0.

steps.label: Substitute and compute · 7/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: For the first input 1.5 and 2.0, substitute step by step: 1 times 1.5, plus 1 times 2.0, plus 0. The sum is drawn as two bars end to end.

steps.label: Substitute and compute · 7/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The result is 3.5. All values were recomputed by program.

steps.label: Substitute and compute · 7/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: For a fixed input, the parameters determine the output.

steps.label: Outputs of the 12 points · 8/9
steps.speakerNotes: On the left are the source's 12 points, each with 2 coordinates. Color matches the output on the right: blue small, orange medium, red large.

steps.label: Outputs of the 12 points · 8/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: On the right are the outputs of the 12 points under the same parameters. The first is 3.5, the maximum is 16, and two outputs coincide.

steps.label: Outputs of the 12 points · 8/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Common misconception: every inner product is a projection length. It is only so for a unit direction; (1,1) is not a unit vector, so the output is a weighted sum, not a projection length. With b nonzero this is an affine mapping; the source uses the broader term linear model.

steps.label: Outputs of the 12 points · 8/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: All 12 outputs were computed by program.

steps.label: What was verified · 9/9
steps.speakerNotes: Matching the arithmetic does not establish task performance. What has been checked: shapes agree and the 12 outputs were recomputed.

steps.label: What was verified · 9/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Here theta is set by interactive controls, with no fitting and no comparison to correct labels, so prediction quality is unchecked.

steps.label: What was verified · 9/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The next unit asks: is the output a category or a continuous value?

steps.label: What was verified · 9/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The note's 4 practice questions stay in the note.
